name: Steve Witkoff

summary.text: Steven C. Witkoff is a New York real-estate investor whom President-elect Donald Trump named Special Envoy to the Middle East on November 12, 2024; in 2025 and 2026 he also led U.S. talks with Russia over the war in Ukraine, meeting Vladimir Putin repeatedly. World Liberty Financial's MiCA whitepaper lists him as a co-founder emeritus who was removed from the company's management body upon taking office; his sons Zach and Alex Witkoff are co-founders of the venture, which Zach runs. The company said in May 2025 that he was divesting; his August 2025 financial disclosure still listed World Liberty Financial among the holdings of Witkoff Holdings LLC, and in September 2026 a new disclosure reported about $107 million in 2025 income from that entity, with the White House saying he had fully divested. In October 2025 eight Senate Democrats wrote to him about the stake and his official dealings with UAE officials.

facts.claim: On November 12, 2024 President-elect Donald Trump announced the appointment of Steven C. Witkoff as Special Envoy to the Middle East, describing him as a leader in business and philanthropy. The envoy post did not require Senate confirmation.

sources.title: Statement by President-elect Donald J. Trump Announcing the Appointment of Steven C. Witkoff as Special Envoy to the Middle East
Trump names golf partner Steve Witkoff as a special envoy to the Middle East

facts.claim: Witkoff's role extended to the Russia-Ukraine war: in February 2025 he sat at the U.S. table for talks with Russia in Saudi Arabia; on April 11, 2025 he met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg in what was reported as their third in-person meeting; and on September 5, 2026 he and Jared Kushner met Putin in Moscow for about three hours before travelling to Kyiv.

facts.claim: World Liberty Financial's MiCA whitepaper lists Steven Witkoff as a co-founder emeritus and states that he was removed from the company's management body upon taking office. His sons Zach and Alex Witkoff are identified as co-founders of the company; Zach Witkoff runs World Liberty Financial.

facts.claim: In May 2025 World Liberty Financial said Witkoff was 'in the process of fully divesting' from the project and had no operational role. His ethics disclosure dated August 13, 2025 showed he had divested a $120 million stake in his real-estate company but still listed World Liberty Financial among the investments held by Witkoff Holdings LLC. In September 2025 a White House spokesperson said he was 'still in the process of divesting'.
facts.quote: Witkoff has since divested a $120 million stake in his real estate company but hasn't yet sold his crypto holdings, according to his most recent ethics disclosure, dated Aug. 13.

sources.title: Adam Schiff, senators, Steve Witkoff, Trump, UAE, World Liberty Financial (Fortune Crypto, Oct. 22, 2025)
US Envoy Steve Witkoff Still Holds Trump-Linked Crypto, Raising Ethics Concerns

facts.claim: On October 22, 2025 Senator Adam Schiff and seven other Senate Democrats wrote to Witkoff asking why he had not divested his World Liberty Financial stake, noting that his August filing listed the company among Witkoff Holdings LLC's investments and had not been signed off by an ethics official, and raising his official meetings with Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose firm MGX had used $2 billion of World Liberty's stablecoin for a Binance investment. The letter is a request for information, not a finding.
facts.quote: Sen. Schiff Leads Senate Democrats in Demanding Answers from Trump Envoy Steve Witkoff on Failure to Divest Ownership of World Liberty Financial Crypto Assets

sources.title: Sen. Schiff Leads Senate Democrats in Demanding Answers from Trump Envoy Steve Witkoff on Failure to Divest Ownership of World Liberty Financial Crypto Assets
Schiff presses Witkoff on divesting from Trump-tied crypto venture

facts.claim: A financial disclosure (OGE Form 278e) reported in September 2026 showed Witkoff received about $107 million in 2025 income from Witkoff Holdings LLC, the entity that held his World Liberty Financial stake, up from about $34 million in 2024; the filing did not break out how much came from World Liberty Financial. White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said Witkoff had fully divested from World Liberty Financial. The sources do not state when the divestment was completed.

facts.claim: In August 2023, before his appointment, the Qatar Investment Authority bought the Park Lane Hotel at 36 Central Park South in Manhattan from a Witkoff-led group for about $623 million, according to property records; Witkoff's group had bought the hotel in 2013 for about $654 million.
facts.quote: The Qatar Investment Authority paid nearly $623 million to acquire the 46-story hotel at 36 Central Park South from Steve Witkoff's company, property records show.

sources.title: Qatar Investment Authority Buys Park Lane Hotel from Witkoff
Qatari Sovereign Wealth Fund Acquires Park Lane Hotel in Manhattan for $623 Million

facts.claim: The New York Times reported that Alex Witkoff pitched a commercial real-estate fund to the Qatar Investment Authority while his father was engaged in hostage negotiations involving Qatar; a QIA spokeswoman confirmed the pitch and said Qatari investors decided not to pursue it, and a Witkoff Group spokeswoman said the preliminary plans had been shelved and disputed other parts of the report as false.
facts.quote: Qatar Investment Authority spokeswoman Melanie Dunn confirmed to the NYT that Alex Witkoff had pitched to the sovereign wealth fund, but affirmed that investors on the Qatari side decided not to pursue the deal.

sources.title: Alex Witkoff sought Qatari funds while his father engaged in hostage negotiations

openQuestions: No source gives the date on which Witkoff's World Liberty Financial interest was sold or transferred; the May 2025 company statement, the August 2025 disclosure and the September 2026 White House statement are the only markers found. The OGE filings themselves were not opened.
The original New York Times report on Alex Witkoff's pitch to the QIA could not be reached; the item rests on a Yahoo Finance relay that quotes the QIA's and Witkoff Group's responses.

Any dealings in Witkoff's envoy role with Qatari or UAE officials tied to World Liberty Financial appear only in the senators' October 2025 letter and in press accounts; no official record of such meetings was found.
Witkoff's exact title changed over 2025-26 (Special Envoy to the Middle East; Special Envoy for Peace Missions per one source); the later title was not confirmed in a primary source.
